unit_description: This unit builds rounding and estimation skills. Students round to the nearest ten and hundred using number lines and place value, then use rounded numbers to estimate and judge reasonable answers.
unit_goals: Round numbers to the nearest ten using a number line.
Round numbers to the nearest hundred using a number line.
Use place value to round numbers.
Identify whether an answer is reasonable.

weeks.weekly_focus: Students learn to round to the nearest ten and hundred, use place-value reasoning, and estimate to check whether answers make sense.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by counting by tens on a number line.
lessons.concept: A number rounds to the nearest ten that is closest on the number line. If it is exactly halfway, round up to the next ten.
lessons.practice: Round two- and three-digit numbers to the nearest ten on a number line.
lessons.objective: Round numbers to the nearest ten.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by finding the nearest ten.

questions.prompt: What is the nearest ten to 27?
What is the nearest ten to 45?
What is the nearest ten to 62?

learn.title: Round to the Nearest Ten
teaching_points: Find the two tens a number is between.
Choose the ten that is closer. If halfway, round up.

example.equation: 37 is between 30 and 40. It is closer to 40.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Round each number to the nearest ten.

bigIdea.title: Round to the Nearest Ten
bigIdea.subtitle: Find the closest ten on the number line
bigIdea.intro: Rounding makes numbers easier to work with. On a number line, rounding to the nearest ten means jumping to the closest ten.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How do you know which ten is closer?

ruleCards.description: First locate the two tens the number is between.
When the ones digit is 5 or more, round up to the next ten.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by counting by hundreds on a number line.
lessons.concept: A number rounds to the nearest hundred that is closest on the number line. The tens digit tells you whether to round up or down.
lessons.practice: Round three- and four-digit numbers to the nearest hundred.
lessons.objective: Round numbers to the nearest hundred.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by finding the nearest hundred.

questions.prompt: What is the nearest hundred to 280?
What is the nearest hundred to 450?
questions.hint: 5 or more in the tens place rounds up.

questions.prompt: What is the nearest hundred to 1,230?

learn.title: Round to the Nearest Hundred
teaching_points: Look at the tens digit to decide.
5 or more in the tens place means round up.

example.equation: 462 is between 400 and 500. The tens digit is 6, so round up to 500.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.hint: The tens digit is 4, so round down.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Round each number to the nearest hundred.

bigIdea.title: Round to the Nearest Hundred
bigIdea.subtitle: Use the tens digit to decide
bigIdea.intro: Rounding to the nearest hundred is like rounding to the nearest ten, but you look at the tens digit to decide which hundred is closer.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: What digit tells you to round up to the next hundred?

ruleCards.description: Look at the tens digit. If it is 5 or more, round up.
If the tens digit is less than 5, keep the hundreds digit the same.

lessons.lesson_title: Use Place Value to Round Numbers
lessons.fact_drill: Round three numbers to the nearest ten and nearest hundred.
lessons.concept: The digit to the right of the place you are rounding to tells you whether to round up or stay the same.
lessons.practice: Round to the nearest ten, hundred, or thousand by looking at the digit to the right.
lessons.objective: Use place value to round numbers to any target place.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by identifying the digit to the right.

questions.prompt: What digit do you look at to round 6,214 to the nearest hundred?
questions.hint: The digit to the right of the hundreds place.

learn.title: Use Place Value to Round Numbers
teaching_points: Find the place you are rounding to.
Look at the digit immediately to the right.
5 or more round up; 4 or less stay the same.

example.equation: The hundreds digit is 3, so 4,358 rounds to 4,000.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.hint: The hundreds digit is 6, so round up.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Round each number to the target place.

flashcards.title: Rounding by Place Value
flashcards.instructions: Review how place value helps you round.

bigIdea.title: Use Place Value to Round Numbers
bigIdea.subtitle: Look at the digit to the right
bigIdea.intro: You can round to any place by looking at the digit one place to the right. That digit tells you whether to round up or stay.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How does place value help you round to larger places?

ruleCards.description: Find the thousands place, then look at the digit to its right.

ruleCards.equation: 6 or more → round up; 4 or less → stay
ruleCards.description: The digit to the right decides the rounding direction.

lessons.fact_drill: Round two numbers and add the rounded numbers mentally.
lessons.concept: Estimate by rounding numbers to friendly places, then compute. Check if an answer is close to the estimate.
lessons.practice: Estimate sums and differences and decide if a given answer is reasonable.
lessons.objective: Use rounding to estimate and judge reasonableness.

questions.prompt: Estimate 48 + 32 by rounding each to the nearest ten.
Estimate 95 - 47 by rounding each to the nearest ten.

learn.title: Estimate and Identify Reasonable Answers
teaching_points: Round each number to a friendly place.
Compare the exact answer to the estimate.

example.equation: 178 ≈ 200 and 156 ≈ 200, so the estimate is 400. 340 is not reasonable.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Estimate 387 + 212 by rounding to the nearest hundred.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Estimate each problem and decide if the given answer is reasonable.

bigIdea.title: Estimate and Identify Reasonable Answers
bigIdea.subtitle: Round first, then judge
bigIdea.intro: Estimation helps you know if an answer makes sense. Round each number, do the easy calculation, and compare.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why is it helpful to estimate before solving?

ruleCards.description: Round to numbers that are easy to add or subtract mentally.
If the exact answer is far from the estimate, check your work.

lessons.fact_drill: Rapid review of rounding to tens, hundreds, and thousands, and estimating answers.
lessons.concept: Review rounding to the nearest ten, hundred, and thousand, and using estimates to judge reasonable answers.
lessons.practice: Complete a balanced evaluation covering the skills from this unit.
lessons.objective: Show what you know about rounding and estimation.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Get ready to show what you know.

questions.hint: 3 is less than 5, so round down.
5 in the tens place rounds up.

learn.title: Ready to Show What You Know
teaching_points: Use a number line if you get stuck.

example.prompt: You have learned four big ideas this unit.
example.equation: round tens + round hundreds + place-value rounding + estimation = rounding and estimation

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Which is 6,247 rounded to the nearest thousand?
try_it.hint: The hundreds digit is 2, so round down.

practice_block.title: Unit Evaluation
practice_block.instructions: Answer all questions carefully to show your understanding.

flashcards.title: Unit 3 Review
flashcards.instructions: Review key terms from Unit 3 before the evaluation.

bigIdea.title: Unit Evaluation: Rounding and Estimation
bigIdea.subtitle: Show what you know
bigIdea.intro: This evaluation checks your understanding of the four big ideas from this unit: rounding to tens, hundreds, any place, and estimating reasonable answers.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: What do you know about rounding and estimation?

ruleCards.equation: Look one place to the right
ruleCards.description: The digit to the right of the target place tells you whether to round up.
Use rounded numbers to check if an exact answer makes sense.
